content_preview.title: PHP Pre-Announces October 21 Security Release for Two Critical Vulnerabilities Rated CVSS v4.0 9.2
content_preview.summary: The PHP security team says a release due October 21 at 14:00 UTC fixes two critical vulnerabilities, both CVSS v4.0 9.2, and urges users to prepare to upgrade.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PHP security team has given advance notice of a security release scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC. According to the [PHP.net homepage](https://www.php.net/index.php), the release "addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2." The notice was dated 20 Oct 2026 and says: "All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available."

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact 398-word Briefing (range 300-800) with Overview / What We Know / Context / What We Don't Know. Clear separation of what the notice states from what is unknown. No analysis overreach.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read from disk (gunzip + text extraction), then live re-fetched. No suspicious_patterns in the manifest for any source. source-0 (https://www.php.net/index.php, 200): front-page news item dated 20 Oct 2026 titled 'Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release' says verbatim 'It is scheduled for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC. It addresses two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2. All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available. We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild. Full details, affected versions, and the fixed versions will be published with the release.' All three quoted fragments in the article are verbatim; 21 October 2026 is a Wednesday. The 'two critical vulnerabilities' and 'CVSS v4.0 9.2' wording appears ONLY on php.net (correctly attributed to it in the article, not to LWN). The same page lists 8.5.11, 8.4.26, 8.3.35, 8.2.34 as current, each with a 24 Sep 2026 'This is a security release' entry (article names 8.4.26 and 8.2.34 and 8.5.11; the 8.3.35 entry is identical, so nothing is contradicted), and the 08 Oct 2026 'PHP 8.6.0 RC3 available for testing' item with the verbatim 'Please DO NOT use this version in production, it is an early test version.' and 'The next release will be RC4, planned for 22 October 2026.' source-1 (https://lwn.net/Articles/1101687/, 200): 'Critical PHP security update coming', posted October 20, 2026 by corbet; says 'there is a high-stakes security update coming at 14:00 UTC on October 21' and 'Anybody running a PHP site probably needs to be prepared for this one.' (verbatim as quoted). LWN does not state the vulnerability count or CVSS values and the article does not claim it does. source-2 (https://github.com/php/php-src/releases/tag/php-8.5.11, 200): PHP 8.5.11 released by adoy 24 Sep 13:57 (datetime 2026-09-24T13:57:18Z, matches the article's timestamp), body 'This is a security release. All PHP 8.5 users are encouraged to upgrade'. The page gives no fix details; the article makes none. 'What We Don't Know' verified: CVE ids, names/components, affected branches and fix contents are genuinely unstated in all three sources (php.net says details and fixed versions come 'with the release'). LIVE RE-FETCH at 2026-10-21 ~08:27 UTC: php.net front page (WebFetch and curl) still shows the 20 Oct notice as the top item and no 8.5.12/8.4.27/8.3.36/8.2.35; the php.net releases Atom feed is last updated 2026-09-24 (8.5.11); GitHub releases/tags top out at php-8.5.11, php-8.4.26, php-8.3.35 (no newer tag). The release had NOT shipped at review time, so the statement that the PHP.net releases page did not yet list it is accurate. Staleness note: the article is dated 21 Oct and is accurate as written as of its publication; if the 14:00 UTC release ships with different CVSS values, counts or branches, that would be later news not a retroactive error. Allowlist: chief:review flagged php.net (www. stripped) as not allowlisted; php.net is the PHP project's own official site, previously cited by the PHP license (May) and 8.6 Beta 3 (Sep) articles (both flagged this same warning), so it was added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment after independent verification of the page content. First-party only: sources are php.net (project), LWN (independent secondary, repeats only the date/time and call to prepare) and GitHub (project repository).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, time, version, quote and attribution traced to a snapshot: 21 Oct 2026 14:00 UTC; 'two critical vulnerabilities'; CVSS v4.0 9.2 (both); notice dated 20 Oct; earlier-release right; 24 Sep security releases (8.5.11, 8.4.26, 8.2.34 named; 8.3.35 also); 8.5.11 timestamp 2026-09-24T13:57:18Z; 8.6.0 RC3 on 08 Oct 2026; RC4 planned 22 Oct 2026; LWN 20 Oct by corbet and its title/quote. The article's 'both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, which it labels critical' is accurate to the notice. No hallucinations found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no alarmism beyond quoted sources; no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers this announcement (no 2026-10 PHP article; 2026-09 Beta 3 and 2026-05 license articles are different topics).
concerns: Single primary source (php.net) for the central claim; mitigated because the claim is a first-party announcement and is clearly attributed. Time-sensitive: the release is due 14:00 UTC on 21 Oct, hours after review; a follow-up article on the actual release would be appropriate.
recommendations: Cover the actual release (CVE ids, affected branches, fixed versions) in a separate follow-up once published.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced pre-announcement Briefing; every quote and figure verified against the raw snapshots and a live re-fetch. Approved without corrections; php.net added to the allowlist. Featured candidacy: 2 - advance notice of a critical-rated security release for PHP, which runs a large share of the web, of broad interest to developers and operators
